title: Marvell's roughly $115B bid for Lumentum sinks both stocks and drags AI networking lower
intro: The week opened with consolidation in AI optics: Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued near $115B, and both shares fell sharply, pulling Astera Labs, Credo and Coherent down with them, while server makers kept sliding ahead of Super Micro's results. Tracked value fell 1.1% between the Oct 30 and Nov 2 closes and 5.2% week over week from Oct 26, with Tokyo Electron, SK hynix and Taiwan test and assembly names among the few gainers as Korean memory makers locked in long-term contracts and ASE raised its packaging outlook.
movers_note: Between the Oct 30 and Nov 2 closes (all 62 names with a new quote) Tokyo Electron (+5.2%), SK hynix (+3.8%), KYEC (+3.7%), Advantest (+2.6%) and Foxconn (+2.2%) rose most, while Lumentum (-18.6%), Marvell (-12.7%), Astera Labs (-11.2%), Intel (-8.8%) and Oracle (-8.8%) fell most; the source's updated share counts lifted several ADR market caps (ASE, UMC, TSMC, ASML) even though their prices slipped.

items.headline: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued near $115B to add AI optics
items.summary: Marvell will exchange 4.5 of its shares for each Lumentum share, a 23.9% premium to the Oct 28 unaffected close, leaving Lumentum holders with about 33% of the combined company. The deal targets a close in the first half of 2028, carries a $3.2B fee if regulators block it, and pits the combined company against Broadcom and Coherent in optical connectivity.

items.headline: Samsung and SK hynix sign long-term memory contracts with 24 customers while pacing new capacity
items.summary: Samsung has long-term agreements with 10 customers and is negotiating with 10 more, while SK hynix has 14 customers on terms of roughly five years. Samsung aims to put 60-70% of its capacity under such contracts by 2030, and both makers are pacing expansion because new fabs could ease supply around 2028.

items.headline: ASE posts record Q3 profit, lifts 2026 capex to $11.5B and expects advanced packaging sales to double in 2027
items.summary: ASE's third-quarter net profit rose 148% from a year earlier to NT$26.996B on sales of NT$244.16B. It added $1B to its capex plan for $11.5B, raised its 2026 leading-edge assembly and test (LEAP) revenue forecast to $4B, and expects that revenue to double in 2027.

items.headline: AI server stocks keep sliding before Super Micro's Nov 3 results despite its $18.5-19.5B preliminary quarter
items.summary: By early afternoon on Nov 2 Super Micro was down about 5%, Dell 4% and HPE 3%, extending a slide that began Oct 30. Super Micro's preliminary fiscal Q1 revenue range is $18.5B-$19.5B, but it guided gross margin to only 10.4%-10.8%, against 17.6% in the prior quarter.

items.headline: Murata plans about ¥1 trillion over five years to expand capacitor output for data-center demand
items.summary: The fiscal 2026-2030 plan splits roughly ¥350B for buildings and ¥650B for equipment, with construction in Okayama starting in April 2027. Murata expects fiscal 2030 MLCC sales to be at least double fiscal 2025, pointing to tight supply of passive components for AI servers.
